claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.8, annual return 9%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits: The strategy uses 'full' operators (zscore_full, winsor_full) which calculate statistics using the entire dataset rather than a rolling window, introducing lookahead bias.

verdict.opinion: The strategy utilizes 'full' operators in its signal construction, which incorporate information from the entire backtest period into each point-in-time calculation. This lookahead bias invalidates the performance metrics, as the model effectively 'knows' the future distribution of returns. While the strategy logic (cross-sectional mean reversion) is sound, the implementation is flawed. I recommend moving to paper trading to verify performance using a strictly point-in-time signal calculation (e.g., replacing 'full' operators with rolling equivalents) before committing real capital.
